goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.
goldens.reasoning: No candidate raises the issue that several goroutines can build the same index at once because the lock was narrowed. C2 brings up the lock change only to explain why the TotalDocs race becomes more likely.

goldens.comment: Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.
goldens.reasoning: C2 describes the same problem: TotalDocs loops over the cache map without a lock while the watcher goroutine can call BuildIndex and write to the map, which can cause a concurrent map access panic.

candidates: pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35 - The storage-server integration test is now skipped on Postgres instead of being fixed.. Every CI run with `GRAFANA_TEST_DB=postgres` now skips this test, so Postgres runs of the storage-server module no longer test it. This PR moves Init into the constructor, which changes startup on every backend, so this is exactly the test that should catch a break. The PR summary calls this "Enhanced PostgreSQL integration test compatibility", but the change only adds a skip. Fix the test for Postgres in Drone, or track the skip in an issue and don't present it as a compatibility fix.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 - The new TotalDocs() call reads the bleve cache map without a lock while indexes can be written into it.. This line runs after the event goroutine has started (lines 208-214). `handleEvent` can call `getOrCreateIndex`, which leads to `BuildIndex` writing `b.cache[key]`. `bleveBackend.TotalDocs` loops over `b.cache` without taking `cacheMu`. If an event for a namespace with no index yet arrives during this call, Go aborts the process with "concurrent map iteration and map write". The lock change in this PR also means writers now hold `cacheMu` only briefly, which makes them more likely to overlap with this read. Take `cacheMu` (ideally an RWMutex read lock) inside `TotalDocs`, or compute the total before starting the watch goroutine.

pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258 - Removing the per-request Init checks also removes the "service is stopping" guard set by Stop.. `Stop` still sets `s.initErr = "service is stopping"`. Before this change, every RPC called `s.Init(ctx)`, which returned that error, so requests that arrived after Stop were rejected. With all of those calls removed, nothing reads `initErr` after construction. Create, Update, Delete, Read, List, Watch, Search and the blob calls that arrive during shutdown now run against a backend whose context has already been cancelled, and its watcher has stopped. Keep a cheap check in each handler, for example an atomic `stopping` flag or a read of `s.initErr`, so these requests still fail fast with a clear error.
